a:r.a:t: Step 4: scanning of the mRNA until an AUG codon is found
Step 5: 60S subunit associates and many of the initiation factors are released.

p:cNvPr.descr: A complex diagram shows the steps in initiation of protein synthesis for eukaryotes. The diagram begins at the top with the 40S subunit and eukaryotic initiation factors. The 40S subunit is cadet blue and shaped like a cup, with an indentation set away from the viewer, divided into the E, P, and A sites. Shown above these sites are eIF1, eIF3, and eIF1A, which are represented by cadet blue sphered of varying sized (eIF1A is more oval-shaped). Arrows below them point down to show that they are about to bind to the E, P, and A sites. Below this image is an arrow pointing down, with (1) on the right. The arrow points down to the next image. The eIF1 binds to the E site, and the eIF1A binds to the A site. The eIF3 is attached to the lower left part of the subunit, slightly to the back. Below this image is an arrow curving down and to the right, labeled (2) on the upper right side. On the left are two convergent arrows. The first shows the addition of tRNA and its anticodon, attached at the top to eIF2, which is a cadet blue sphere as well. The tRNA is represented by a tightly curled green molecule, bonded at its amino acid arm at the top to Met, which is a light blue sphere. The tRNA has a yellow portion at the bottom, with UAC written on it. This is the anticodon (3' to 5'). The second convergent arrow, below, shows the addition of eIF5B bonded right to GTP. eIF5B is also a cadet blue sphere. The arrow points right to the next image, which consists of the 40S subunit with the tRNA attached to the eIF2-GTP in its P site, the eIF1 sitting just above the E site but not fully settled inside, and eIF1A in the A site, bonded above to eIF5B-GTP. The eIF3 is still bonded to the bottom left of the 40S, toward the back. The whole complex is labeled "43S preinitiation complex" at the right. Above this image is a curved arrow pointing up. It is labeled (3) on the left. On the left side of the arrow there is a convergent arrow showing the addition of an mRNA strand, carried by eIF4F. The eIF4F is cadet blue and is canoe-shaped for transport. The mRNA's 5' end, on the left, has a red sequence, and then the remainder is green, except for a dark green sequence labeled AUG. To the right of AUG there is a break in the strand, then the 3' end. On the right side of the arrow is a convergent-divergent arrow showing addition of ATP and removal of ADP + Pi. The arrow points up to the next image, which consists of the 40S subunit with all previously described initiation factors and the tRNA, plus the eIF4F attached to the front of the 40S. The mRNA follows the curve of the E, P, and A sites, then slopes downward off the 40S and flattens out. The whole complex is labeled the 48S complex on the right. Above this image is an arrow curving up and to the right. It is labeled (4) on the bottom and "scanning" above. The arrow points right to the next image, which consists of the 48S complex, with a much longer mRNA strand. The red sequence at the end now loops down and to the left, attaching at the far left end of the eIF4F. The dark green AUG sequence is aligned with the yellow UAC anticodon on the tRNA. Below this image is an arrow curving downward, labeled (5) on the left. There is a divergent arrow on the left showing removal of the eIFB-GDP + Pi, eIF2-GDP + Pi, and eIF1. On the right, there is a divergent arrow showing removal of the eIF3 and eIF1A. Finally, on the right near the bottom, there is a convergent arrow showing addition of the 60S subunit. The arrow points down to the final complex. The 40S subunit still has the tRNA attached to its P site, and the mRNA on its front. The AUG aligns underneath the UAC on the anticodon. The EIF4F is to the left of the subunit, with the 5' end of the mRNA. Above the 40S subunit is the 60S subunit, which is a very large pink subunit shaped like a mushroom cap, with corresponding E, P, and A sites on its undersite. The tRNA fits into the P site on the 60S subunit as well. The whole structure is bracketed on the right and labeled 80S.
